references.Davis 1894: Davis, C. H. S. The Egyptian Book of the Dead: The Most Ancient and the Most Important of the Extant Religious Texts of Ancient Egypt. New York and London: G. P. Putnam's Sons, 1894. (English version of Pierret's French translation of P. Turin 1791.) https://sites.dlib.nyu.edu/viewer/books/ifa_egypt000060 - Davis was a starting point, but translations were later changed to reflect more recent scholarship, although certain archaisms like 'Netherworld' were kept
references.Faulkner 1990: Faulkner, R. O. The Ancient Egyptian Book of the Dead. London: British Museum Press, 1990.
references.Weber 2022: Weber, F. "Thematic Groups and Sequences of Spells." In R. Lucarelli and M. A. Stadler (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of the Egyptian Book of the Dead, 341–356. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2022.
references.Lucarelli 2022: Lucarelli, R. "Gods and Demons in the Book of the Dead: The Gods of the Netherworld between Myth and Funerary Religion." In R. Lucarelli and M. A. Stadler (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of the Egyptian Book of the Dead, 421–432. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2022.

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling the crocodiles which come to seize the magic of a person in the Netherworld.
The crocodiles menacingly side-eye you.
descriptions.settled: The crocodiles menacingly side-eye you, but you've rendered them impotent to do much else.

caption_e32.name: Spell 32

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling the crocodiles which come to seize the magic of the glorious spirit in the Netherworld.

caption_e32.reference: This referes to the 'akh' spirit, translated as glorious mostly for simplicity.

descriptions.default: The crocodiles eye you covetously, eager for a meal.
descriptions.settled: The crocodiles stare into the spear, adequately cowed.

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling all snakes.
A large snake makes its presence known.
descriptions.settled: The snake accepts the imposing presence of the spear.

descriptions.default: Spell for not being eaten by any snake in the Netherworld.
A snake lies on the ground.
descriptions.settled: The snakes have been turned away.

caption_e36.name: Spell 36

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling the flesh eating insects.

caption_e36.reference: 'apshait' is a somewhat uncertain insect. The TLA only describes it as an insect, possible a roach, a beetle (Faulkner 1990), a cockroach (because of numerous illustrations of it). It is most likely some flesh eating insect (necrophagous beetle belonging in the dermestidae family), explaining why one might need to protect against it in death (Meeks 2010, 290).

descriptions.default: The flesh eating insects scurry around your feet.
descriptions.settled: Begone from me, crooked lips! They lie dead at your feet.

caption_e37.name: Spell 37

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling the two Merety snakes.

caption_e37.reference: Faulkner 1990 calls it songstress snakes; Weber 2022, 347, calles them the the 'two goddesses, the Merety,' often shown as snakes. The FCD (Faulkner's Concise Dictionary) cites 'Mrt' as 'musician-goddess'

e37.name: The two Merety snakes

descriptions.default: One Meret snake looks away from you deceitfully. That seems like one snake less than there should be...
descriptions.settled: The duplicated Merety snakes show as one again, thoroughly beat.

e37.reference: Davis 1894; Weber 2022 (the Merety, two goddesses often shown as snakes); the rest is game text

caption_e38.name: Spell 38

descriptions.default: Spell for living by air in the Netherworld which is said to repel snakes.

caption_e38.reference: A modification was made as the text actually says 'to repel the two Merety snakes' but was modified for the sake of gameplay to be more general

descriptions.default: The signs of life and breath are offered to you. Only one can be taken.

caption_e39.name: Spell 39

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling the serpent Apep in the Netherworld.

caption_e39.reference: Faulkner 1990, 60, says 'a rerek-snake', but the text is 'rfrf' (??), other references also calls it Rerek; text was changed to say 'Apep' for game play, as the spell addresses Apep, and Rerek is known to be another name or a sort of replacement snake for Apep (Apophis). In Lucarelli 2022, 430, but I feel like also somewhere else.

e39.name: Apep

descriptions.default: Apep saunters leglessly across the road.
descriptions.settled: Apep sulks with greatly diminished amplitude.

e39.reference: Davis 1894; Lucarelli 2022 (Apophis, with Rerek as an earlier form); the rest is game text

caption_e40.name: Spell 40

descriptions.default: Spell for repelling the Eater of the Ass.

caption_e40.reference: Faulkner 1990, 61, kind of, but keepiong Davis 1894's phrasing, 'Eater of the Ass' is a banger name, better than 'him who swallowed an ass'

descriptions.default: A snake slides along the donkey's back, thinking of lunch. The Eater of the Ass.
descriptions.settled: The Eater did not live up to its name, and ate no ass.

caption_e41.name: Spell 41

descriptions.default: Spell for preventing the slaughtering of a man in the Netherworld.

caption_e41.reference: This is a vertebrae! See Gardiner F41, 'from an old sign depicting stalks of flax tied together and the bolls cut off.'

descriptions.default: Something stirs inside the sheaf.
descriptions.settled: The snake is pinned on top of the sheaf, exactly where it hoped not to be.
